items.text: Marriage should be open to any two adults, whatever their sex.
items.rationale: Core progressive/liberal-egalitarian position on marriage recognition; mirror of pro-10. Answerable in both frames, and people may split where local law differs from their ideal.

items.text: If one partner no longer wants to stay married, they should be able to divorce without proving the other did wrong.
items.rationale: No-fault divorce, endorsed by progressives and many liberals; the condition (an unwilling partner) favours the progressive pole. Mirror of pro-09; reads the same in both frames.

items.text: A person's legal gender should be whatever they declare it to be, with no medical requirements.
items.rationale: Gender self-identification, a strong progressive stance (level 3); mirror of pro-11. Recognition, not enforcement. Some may back it as an ideal but want safeguards here and now.

items.text: Abortion should be available to any woman who asks for it in early pregnancy.
items.rationale: Pro-choice position (abortion on request, early term), held by mainstream progressives and feminists; mirror of pro-12. Clear in both frames.
items.note: Framed as availability (what society provides and recognises), not criminal penalties, to keep it off the Liberty-Security axis.

items.text: If a child has two mothers or two fathers, schools should present that family as just as normal as any other.
items.rationale: Institutional affirmation of same-sex-parent families, a progressive view; the condition (a real child in class) favours that pole. Mirror of pro-08; works in both frames.

items.text: Social customs deserve respect only when they treat everyone as equals.
items.rationale: Egalitarian test for custom: custom has no authority of its own. Progressives and rationalist liberals endorse it; Burkean/Confucian traditionalists reject it. Mirror of pro-13.

items.text: If a custom gives men authority over women, it should be openly condemned as unjust.
items.rationale: Strong feminist/egalitarian stance on patriarchal customs; the condition favours the progressive pole, and complementarian traditionalists would disagree. Mirror of pro-14 in strength.

items.text: If a child cannot be raised by its birth parents, it should go to a married mother and father where possible.
items.rationale: Traditional preference for mother-father adoptive homes, held by religious and secular family conservatives; the condition (a child needing a home) favours that pole. Mirror of pro-05.

items.text: If a couple has young children and there is no abuse, they should stay married even when the marriage is unhappy.
items.rationale: Family-conservative view that marriage is a lasting duty to children; the condition (young children, no abuse) favours the traditional pole. Mirror of pro-02; reads the same in both frames.

items.text: Marriage should be a union of one man and one woman.
items.rationale: Classic traditional definition of marriage, shared by many religious and cultural conservatives worldwide; mirror of pro-01. People may split where local law differs from their ideal.

items.text: A person's legal sex should always be the sex they were born with.
items.rationale: Strong sex-realist/traditional stance, endorsed by social conservatives and some gender-critical feminists; mirror of pro-03 at level 3. Recognition, not enforcement.

items.text: Abortion should be allowed only in serious cases, such as rape or a threat to the mother's life.
items.rationale: Mainstream pro-life position with exceptions (not a total ban, so level 2), held by many religious and secular conservatives; mirror of pro-04. Clear in both frames.
items.note: Kept to what is permitted, not to penalties, so it stays off the Liberty-Security axis.

items.text: Customs handed down over many generations deserve respect even when people cannot explain their purpose.
items.rationale: Burkean/Chestertonian and Confucian view that inherited custom carries accumulated wisdom; adherents would recognise it. Mirror of pro-06; frame-neutral.

items.text: If shared customs help hold a community together, its members should be expected to follow them, even against personal preference.
items.rationale: Strong communitarian-traditionalist stance that the community comes before individual choice; the condition (customs bind the community) favours this pole. Social expectation, not legal enforcement. Mirror of pro-07 in strength.
